findings.title: R79-C2's frozen predicate and counting_command omit --battery, and the frozen instrument exits 2 on them
findings.evidence: argv `python3 -I -B tools/round-79/pointer-bind.py --root . --rev <rev> --json-out <receipt>` against the bytes at ed68cd0a exits 2, prints 'usage: --battery --rev <rev> [--json-out <path>] [--control path-only]' on stderr and writes no receipt; the same argv at base 29d2ca30 also exits 2. With --battery added the freeze arm exits 0 (5/5/0/0) and the base arm exits 1 (5/3/2), so every number in the claim is true of the command-with-flag and false of the command-as-printed.
findings.in_flight: The worktree at measurement carries an uncommitted edit by another seat making --rev imply --battery (git status ' M tools/round-79/pointer-bind.py', sha256 3f07bd2a... vs pinned 91d23dad...). HEAD and the freeze still carry the pinned bytes. This seat did not touch it.

findings.title: --validate is a consistency check, not an admission check
findings.evidence: It returns defects [] (exit 0) for the red base receipts (c1-at-base survivors 3, c2-at-base mismatches 2), for the C1 empty-set control (mutants 0, survivors 0) and for the C2 path-only control it returns 10 defects only because a control row legitimately has no line binding. 'A defect-free validate' therefore adds nothing to either predicate and cannot be pointed at as evidence.

findings.title: A missing receipt file exits 1, the same status as a false claim
findings.evidence: Both --validate paths do json.loads(open(path)) with no guard: /nonexistent.json raises FileNotFoundError and the process exits 1. Exit 2 exists in both instruments but is only reachable from argparse and Unevaluable, never from an unreadable receipt.

findings.title: Neither receipt records argv or --root
findings.evidence: The receipt schemas carry target{path,rev,bytes,sha256} / record{path,rev,sha256} but no argv, no root and no instrument self-digest. A receipt therefore cannot be tied to the counting command printed in claims.json, and cannot prove which instrument revision produced it without a separate pin.

findings.title: The single-occurrence edit rule is not carried into the C1 receipt
findings.evidence: apply_mutant refuses text.count(anchor) != 1, but the receipt stores only applied:true and apply_note:'applied'. The anchor, the replacement and the occurrence count are absent, so 'eight exact single-occurrence edits' is assertable only from the instrument table, not from the receipt.

findings.title: killed_by_declared is a dead field
findings.evidence: judge() sets killed_by_declared = killed unconditionally, and killed already requires the declared case to be present and false, so the field can never differ from killed.

findings.title: The C2 base arm is unpinned by construction and the predicate does not say so
findings.evidence: TARGET_SHA256 is the freeze-time digest of tools/round-78/attack-gate.py; at base 29d2ca30 the file differs, so target_pin.matched is false on the base receipt. The C1 base clause claims only survivors 3, so this is not a falsehood, but a validator that requires pin.matched on every arm would reject the base arm.

findings.title: pointer-bind's --rev scopes only the record, not the pointed files
findings.evidence: read_lines() opens expand(path) on the live filesystem; --rev selects PROVINCE.md via git show. The five pointed objects ($HOME configs, Ghidra properties, .bashrc) are always read as they are on disk now, which is the intended freshness semantics but is not stated in the predicate.

findings.title: Round-78 wave accounting is off by one in its membership clause
findings.evidence: seats 12, non-empty outputs 11, evidence dirs 10. The sentence's bins (10 substantive / 1 progress / 1 truncated) sum to 12 and the counts hold, but CriticClaims (2133 B, no dir) must be inside 'substantive evidence (all files under .ufo/waves/round-78/w1/)' while ExecSurfaceProbe (0 B, dir present) is the truncated one. Two seats have no evidence dir; the sentence names one.

findings.title: The freeze gate cannot see S1
findings.evidence: auth_findings checks instrument path+sha256 at the receipt rev only (tools/round-78/attack-gate.py:534-551); it never runs the predicate. The round-79 entry is therefore correctly CLEAN under its own rule while the predicate it audits is unrunnable as printed.

risks: S1 is being repaired in an uncommitted worktree edit by another seat; if the L1 lands it, the instrument digest changes and the freeze pin 91d23dad... no longer resolves, which needs a supersession entry rather than a silent edit.

Re-running any receipt now from the worktree would exercise the modified pointer-bind.py, not the pinned bytes; my measurements were taken while the worktree still matched the pin (verified before the edit appeared).
S2 means a green validate on a red receipt is easy to mislabel as admission; any reviewer reading 'validate defect-free' as corroboration is reading a tautology.
